sections.content: How many people stayed in Billingham after gaining qualifications?

Billingham is a medium-sized town in the North East. Billingham does not have its own university.

Billingham has higher levels of deprivation.

Overall, Billingham ended up with:

  • fewer graduates than it produced
  • a similar number of non-graduates with advanced qualifications as it produced
Note: all towns and cities in this analysis are defined based on population size only. This means that some cities are classed as towns because of their population.

Let's explore this further

There were 1,920 state-school pupils from Billingham who sat their GCSEs between the 2007 to 2008 and the 2010 to 2011 school years.

Of these, 560 (29%) went on to gain degree-level qualifications (level 6+ as defined by The Office of Qualifications and Examinations Regulation, or Ofqual ). We will call these people graduates.

Another 635 (33%) went on to gain other advanced post-16 qualifications, such as A-Levels, a foundation degree or higher apprenticeship (levels 3-5 as defined by Ofqual). In this tool, we will refer to these non-graduates with advanced qualifications as “qualified non-graduates", for brevity.

The charts below compare Billingham to other English towns and cities using three measures:

  • what proportion of Billingham's pupils became graduates or qualified non-graduates by the 2017 to 2018 academic year
  • of those graduates and qualified non-graduates, the percentages that lived in Billingham in the 2018 to 2019 academic year
  • how many graduates and qualified non-graduates from elsewhere came to live there by 2018 to 2019, relative to the number who sat their GCSEs there

In some towns, some of this information may not be available because of small sample sizes.
The size and deprivation level of a town, as well as the qualification levels of older residents, were all related to students' educational attainment. Read our previous analysis.

Where did those who left Billingham move to?

Of Billingham's graduates, 195 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 55 of those graduates (28%) were living fairly locally, in the Middlesbrough and Stockton travel to work area (TTWA).

Of Billingham's qualified (level 3+) non-graduates, 150 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 100 of those qualified non-graduates (67%) were living fairly locally, in the Middlesbrough and Stockton travel to work area (TTWA).

Of those in Billingham's GCSE cohort:

  • 115 graduates left the North East
  • the most common region they moved to was London
  • 35 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates left the North East

In 2018 to 2019, 16% of graduates and 17% of qualified non-graduates living in Billingham had moved there from elsewhere

In the 2018 to 2019 academic year, there were 430 graduates and 580 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates from our cohort living in Billingham. This is compared with the 560 graduates and 635 qualified non-graduates who had lived there when they sat their GCSEs.

In 2018 to 2019, 84% of the graduates had also lived in Billingham as GCSE pupils, while 16% had moved there from elsewhere.

Of the qualified non-graduates who lived in Billingham in 2018 to 2019, 84% had lived there as GCSE pupils, while 17% had moved to the area from elsewhere.
